reasons: Main export, download and erasure paths are covered.
Document, family member and storage deletion are not covered.
Tests use fake database calls, so they do not prove the real queries work.
The token revocation check is set up but not asserted.

terms.meaning: The test runner that executes these checks and reports pass or fail.
A stand-in function that returns a set result, so a test can control what the code sees.
India's data protection law that gives users rights over their personal data.
Deleting or removing a user's personal data at their request.
Replacing identifying details, such as name and email, with placeholders.
Marking a record as deleted and keeping it in the database, rather than removing it.
A stored record of important actions, kept for privacy and security reviews.
A small, temporary version of the app built only for tests.

used_by: Run by the Jest test runner, not imported by app code

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the tests
sections.what: Brings in the testing tools, the exceptions the service throws, the service under test, the fake database and helper pieces, and the revoke reason type.
sections.why: Likely reason: each test file loads what it touches.

sections.name: ComplianceService (DPDP Right to Access & Erasure) (part 1)
sections.title: Fake database and helper setup
sections.what: Creates a fake database in which each table the service uses has stub functions, returning empty results or zero counts by default. Also creates fake password and token checkers.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets each test control exactly what the database returns without a real database.
sections.watch_out: If the service starts using a new table or call that is not stubbed here, the test will fail because the stub is missing.

sections.name: ComplianceService (DPDP Right to Access & Erasure) (part 2)
sections.title: Test module and export request test
sections.what: Builds the testing module with the service and fakes. Checks that a data export creates a request, gathers the user's data, marks the request complete with a download link, and writes an audit entry.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the main export path works from start to finish inside the service.
sections.watch_out: The test checks that a download link is saved, but does not check that the link works.

sections.name: ComplianceService (DPDP Right to Access & Erasure) (part 3)
sections.title: Export download and wrong password tests
sections.what: Checks that asking for an export not owned by the user is refused. Checks that a valid export returns data and logs a download audit entry. Checks that erasure with a wrong password is refused and does not update the user record.
sections.why: Likely reason: protects against one user getting another user's data and against erasure without a correct password.
sections.watch_out: The wrong-password test only checks the user record update. It does not check that other tables were left alone.

sections.name: ComplianceService (DPDP Right to Access & Erasure) (part 4)
sections.title: Successful erasure test
sections.what: Checks that with the correct password, the user's name, email and phone are replaced, the account is marked inactive and deleted, sessions and refresh tokens are removed, and an erasure audit entry is written.
sections.why: Likely reason: this states the outcome the erasure must produce, so it is checked directly.
sections.watch_out: The token service fake is set up but the erasure code shown removes sessions directly and does not call it, so changes in token handling would not be caught here.

summary: Automated checks that data export and account erasure work as the DPDP rules require, using fake database calls instead of a real database.
purpose: Confirms that an export is created and completed, that another user's export cannot be downloaded, that erasure needs the correct password, and that a valid erasure anonymizes the account and removes sessions and tokens.
why: Likely reason: erasure is destructive and legally sensitive, so tests protect it. Fake database calls keep the tests fast and safe.
how: 1. Builds a fake database where each table has stub functions with default results. 2. Builds fake password and token checkers. 3. Creates the testing module with the real service. 4. Runs each scenario, setting the results each one needs and checking which calls were made.
inputs: No outside input. Each test sets the fake results it needs.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: Fake calls may not match the real database, so tests can pass while the real queries fail. Document deletion, family member deletion and file storage deletion are not checked. The fake token service is set up but not checked, and the erasure code shown does not call it.
debug: Run the Jest test for this file. Read the failing expectation message. After changing the service, check that the stubs cover any new database calls. If a toHaveBeenCalledWith check fails, compare the printed arguments with the expected ones.
